spec: Given a string s, split it into a list of sentences, treating '.', '!' and '?' as sentence-ending punctuation. Each returned sentence has its leading and trailing whitespace stripped and does not include the terminating punctuation mark; empty sentences produced by consecutive punctuation or trailing text are omitted from the result.
visible_tests: assert split_into_sentences('Hello there. How are you? Fine!') == ['Hello there', 'How are you', 'Fine']
assert split_into_sentences('One sentence only') == ['One sentence only']

spec: Given a string s, drop every non-alphabetic character and then group the remaining letters into a list of maximal runs of consecutive letters sharing the same case (all uppercase or all lowercase), preserving order. A string with no letters at all returns an empty list.

Given a string s, return the shortest substring that, when repeated a whole number of times, exactly reconstructs s. If no such shorter substring exists (s does not consist of a smaller repeated unit), return s itself unchanged. An empty string returns an empty string.

Given a string s, return True if s can be formed by repeating some strictly shorter substring two or more times (that is, s is not made up only of a repeating unit equal to itself). Return False for an empty string or a string with no such shorter repeating unit.

Given a string s, find its smallest repeating unit (the shortest substring that repeats a whole number of times to reconstruct s), and return how many times that unit repeats. If s has no shorter repeating unit, return 1. An empty string returns 0.

Given a string s and an integer k, find every distinct substring of length k that occurs more than once in s (occurrences may overlap), and return them as a list in the order each first appears. If k is 0, negative, or greater than the length of s, return an empty list.

Given a string s, compute the sum of the alphabetical position of each letter it contains (a or A = 1, b or B = 2, ..., z or Z = 26), ignoring case and skipping any character that is not a letter. An empty string or one with no letters returns 0.

Given a string s, considering only its alphabetic characters in order and ignoring case, return True if each successive letter is strictly later in the alphabet than the one immediately before it. A string with fewer than two letters is always considered increasing.

Given a string s, split it on whitespace into words, and for each word compute the sum of the alphabetical positions of its letters (a=1..z=26, case-insensitive), skipping any non-letter characters within the word. Return the list of per-word sums in the order the words appear; an empty string returns an empty list.

Given a string s, return a list of (character, position) tuples, one for every alphabetic character in s in order, where position is its 1-indexed alphabetical position (a or A = 1 up to z or Z = 26). Non-letter characters are skipped entirely and do not appear in the result.

Given a phrase, split it on whitespace into words and build an acronym string from the uppercase first letter of each word, in order. A word whose first character is not a letter contributes nothing to the acronym. An empty or all-whitespace phrase returns an empty string.

Given a string s made up of words separated by single spaces (no leading, trailing, or doubled spaces), return a list of the indices in s at which each word begins, in order, starting with index 0 for the first word. An empty string returns an empty list.

Given an acronym string and a phrase, return True if the phrase has exactly as many words (split on whitespace) as there are characters in acronym, and each word's first letter matches the corresponding character of acronym, ignoring case. Otherwise return False.
visible_tests: assert is_acronym_match('ASAP', 'as soon as possible') == True

spec: Given a camelCase or PascalCase string s, build an acronym consisting of the first character of s (converted to uppercase) followed by every subsequent uppercase letter found in s, in order. An empty string returns an empty string.

Given two strings a and b, return a sorted list of the distinct characters that appear in both a and b, based purely on which characters each string contains (not how many times). An empty result is returned if the strings share no characters.
Given two strings a and b, return a sorted list of the distinct characters that appear in a but do not appear anywhere in b. An empty result is returned if every character of a also appears in b.
Given a string s, return the sum of all its digit characters interpreted as individual digits 0-9, ignoring any non-digit characters. A string with no digits returns 0.

Given a string s, extract every digit character from s in order, concatenate them into a single sequence of digits, and return that sequence interpreted as an integer. A string with no digits returns 0.

Given a string s, consider only its digit characters in order (ignoring all non-digit characters, which do not break adjacency between digits) and count the number of adjacent digit pairs where the second digit is strictly greater than the first. A string with fewer than two digits returns 0.
Given a string s, split it into a tuple of two strings representing its first half and second half. If the length of s is odd, the extra middle character goes into the first half.

Given a string s and a positive integer k, split s into consecutive blocks of k characters (the final block may be shorter than k), reverse the characters within each block independently, and join the reversed blocks back together in their original order.

Given a string s and an integer n, return s rotated right by n positions, meaning the last n characters are moved to the front of the string. n may be negative or larger than the length of s; the effective rotation should be computed modulo the length of s. An empty string always returns an empty string.

Given a string s, return the length of the longest contiguous substring in which no two adjacent characters are equal. An empty string returns 0, and a string with all distinct adjacent characters returns its full length.

Given a string s and an integer k, count the number of distinct substrings of length exactly k that occur anywhere in s (each distinct substring counted once, regardless of how often it repeats). If k is 0, negative, or greater than the length of s, return 0.
Given a string s, return True if no character appears more than once in s (all characters are distinct), and False otherwise. An empty string returns True.

Given a string s, scan it from left to right and return the first character encountered that has already appeared earlier in the string. Return None if no character repeats anywhere in s, including for an empty string.
Given a string s and a two-character string pair, count the number of positions in s (allowing overlaps) where the substring pair occurs. If s has fewer than two characters, return 0.

Given a string s and a list of strings words, return True if s is a suffix of at least one string in words (a string is always considered a suffix of itself, and the empty string is a suffix of every string). Return False if words is empty.

Given a string s and a single character ch, remove exactly the first occurrence and the last occurrence of ch from s (if ch occurs only once, remove just that single instance), leaving all other characters, including any other occurrences of ch, in place. If ch does not appear in s, return s unchanged.

Given a string s and a list of integer indices, return s with the characters at those positions removed (referring to positions in the original string). Indices may be given in any order, may repeat, and any index outside the valid range of s is simply ignored.

Given a string s, a single character ch, and a positive integer n, return the index of the nth occurrence (1-indexed) of ch in s, scanning left to right. Return -1 if ch occurs fewer than n times in s, including when s is empty.

Given a string s and a single character ch, find all positions where ch occurs in s and return a list of the gaps (index differences) between each pair of consecutive occurrences, in order. If ch occurs fewer than two times, return an empty list.

Given a string s, return True if for every valid position i, the character at position i is equal to the character at position i+2 (the string repeats with a period of 2 when comparing characters two apart). Strings of length 0, 1, or 2 always satisfy this and return True.
Given a string s, return the number of distinct characters that appear anywhere in s, regardless of how many times each one repeats. An empty string returns 0.

Given a string s, a target width, and a single fill character fillchar, center s within a field of the given width using fillchar for padding. If the padding needed cannot be split evenly between both sides, the extra fill character goes on the right side. If width is less than or equal to the length of s, return s unchanged.

Given a string s and an integer max_len (at least 3), if s is longer than max_len characters, truncate it and append an ellipsis '...' so that the returned string has exactly max_len characters in total; otherwise return s unchanged.

Given a string s, return True if it is valid kebab-case: made up only of lowercase letters and digits grouped into non-empty segments separated by single hyphens, with no leading or trailing hyphen and no two consecutive hyphens. Return False for an empty string or any string violating these rules (such as containing uppercase letters, spaces, or other punctuation).

Given a string s, return True if it is valid snake_case: made up only of lowercase letters and digits grouped into non-empty segments separated by single underscores, with no leading or trailing underscore and no two consecutive underscores. Return False for an empty string or any string violating these rules (such as containing uppercase letters, spaces, or other punctuation).

Given a string s made of words separated by underscores and/or spaces, convert it to kebab-case: lowercase every letter and replace each run of one or more underscores or spaces with a single hyphen; leading and trailing separators are removed entirely.

Given a camelCase or PascalCase string s, convert it to snake_case by inserting an underscore before each uppercase letter (except when it is the very first character of the string) and lowercasing every letter.
